decision: Keep best021; all six fixed candidate arms failed the development advancement gate.
matched_control: Both adaptation arms begin at the same 100-epoch head and run the same 12 epochs/240 updates, sample orders, head LR, dropout seed. Compute time is not matched because last-stage backpropagation costs more.
result: Last-stage adaptation lowers training RMSE but worsens overall standalone and fixed-10-percent blend OOF for both architectures relative to the matched head-only control.
limitations: Only this fixed 100+12 epoch training protocol was tested; no claim of full convergence or architecture ceiling.
Long-reused development400 and conditional bootstrap are not an independent validation set or selection-adjusted evidence.
Native full256 and official normalization were used; official enum default resize/crop were intentionally not used.

Swin saved-checkpoint CPU/MPS reload passes, but exact full training replay fails. Same-label same-seed repetition also differs, consistent with numerical execution nondeterminism; the responsible kernel/root cause was not proved.
